questions.prompt: A team tests a new prompt on the five inputs they used while writing it, sees perfect results, and ships. Why is this risky?

options.text: Five inputs take too long to run
The test set is tiny and identical to the development examples, so it measures memory rather than quality
Perfect results are always a bug
Prompts can't be tested before shipping

questions.explanation: Use a larger set drawn from real inputs, with edge cases, kept separate from the examples used to build the prompt.

questions.prompt: Which practices reduce LLM-as-a-judge bias? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use a clear rubric with separate criteria
Swap answer order in pairwise comparisons
Grade with a different model from the one that generated the output

questions.explanation: Rubrics, order swapping, a different grading model, and calibration against humans counter known biases. Preferring longer answers is itself the verbosity bias.

questions.prompt: Re-running your evaluation after every prompt or model change to catch anything that got worse is called ____ testing.
questions.explanation: Regression tests ensure a fix for one case doesn't silently break others.

questions.prompt: Which is one of Anthropic's three principles for designing evaluations?

options.text: Prefer a few hand-graded cases over many automated ones
Prioritize volume over quality: more automated cases beat a few hand-graded ones
Avoid edge cases to keep scores high

questions.explanation: The guide's principles are: be task-specific (with edge cases), automate when possible, and prioritize volume over quality.

questions.prompt: Match each LLM-judge bias to its description.

pairs.right: Favoring the first or second answer by order
Favoring longer answers even when not better
Favoring answers from itself or similar models
Checking judge scores against human labels

questions.explanation: Knowing each bias tells you which mitigation to apply; calibration confirms the judge is trustworthy.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of building an evaluation for a prompt.

items.text: Run it on every change as a regression test
Build a test set with real and edge cases

questions.explanation: Define what good means, collect representative cases, decide how to grade, then run it continuously.
